group: bouncer over a chaotic block list (exp/sqrt), not solved
title: What is known about 1RB1RA_1RC0RF_1RD0RD_1LE---_0LC1LF_1RA0LE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RA_1RC0RF_1RD0RD_1LE---_0LC1LF_1RA0LE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The run is a bouncer over a list of blocks of 1s, with a list that changes in a chaotic way. Lean proves only the sweep rules; the description of the list comes from simulation.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: B with 0 under the head, 1 two right. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 47,708 cells have been visited and 37,559 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.503). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.089).

claims.title: 4 sweep rules, for all n
claims.text: The head crosses a run of n copies of a short word in one go, for all n and any tape around it.

claims.title: A list of blocks
claims.text: A C run of 10<sup>9</sup> steps: whenever the head extends the tape on the right in state A the tape is a list of blocks of 1s separated by single 0s; the last time (774,448,167 steps) it has 5317 blocks: 2632 of length 3, 1352 of length 7, 658 of length 11, 329 of length 15, 165 of length 19, 91 of length 23, 50 of length 27, and a few others. Lengths 4m + 3, about half as many of each length as of the one before.

claims.title: Sweeps and a growing end block
claims.text: Between those events the head goes from the right part to the left end and back again; at the left end it adds cells, and the leftmost block grows by 4 cells per sweep (29, 33, 37, 41, 45 around step 3 × 10<sup>7</sup>) until it is rewritten by a later sweep.

claims.title: Growth
claims.text: Since each sweep crosses the whole left part and adds a few cells there, the left side grows like the square root of the step count; the right end grows only in rare bursts, like the logarithm.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The block list is rewritten in a way that looks chaotic; no round map and no invariant are known.

claims.text: The same table as 1RB---_0RC1RD_1LA0LA_1LE0RB_1LF1LE_1LC0LD up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0RE_1RC0RC_1LD---_0LB1LE_1RF0LD_1RA1RF up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0RB_1LC---_0LA1LD_1RE0LC_1RF1RE_1RA0RD up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine runs back and forth over a list of blocks of 1s, rewriting it on every pass, and the list it leaves looks random: about half the blocks have length 3, a quarter length 7, an eighth length 11, and so on. This page runs the real machine and lists what is known.

facts.text: Sweep rules proved in Lean for all n.
Length of the block list after about 7.7 × 10<sup>8</sup> steps.
No halt in the C simulator.

sections.heading: A list of blocks
html: Whenever the head extends the tape on the right in state A, the tape is a list of blocks of 1s separated by single 0s. The last such moment in a 109-step run, at step 774,448,167, the list has 5317 blocks: 2632 of length 3, 1352 of length 7, 658 of length 11, 329 of length 15, 165 of length 19, 91 of length 23, 50 of length 27, and a few others. So lengths are 4m + 3, with about half as many blocks of each length as of the one before, as if the lengths were random.

sections.heading: A bouncer that rewrites
html:
The head sweeps from the right part of the tape to the left end and back. At the left end it adds cells, and the leftmost block grows by 4 cells per sweep until it is rewritten by a later sweep; on the way the sweeps rewrite the blocks they pass. The sweeps are built from runs the head crosses in one go, which Lean proves for all lengths (for example L A> (1)^n R to L (1)^n A> R).

The left side therefore grows like the square root of the step count; the right side grows only in rare bursts, roughly at a constant ratio of the step count, like a logarithm.

sections.heading: How it would halt
html: The only halting transition is D1, and D is entered only from C, which always moves right. So the machine halts exactly when the head, in state C, steps right onto a 1. In the block list this would need a particular local pattern that the sweeps have not produced so far; no argument says they never will.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB---_0RC1RD_1LA0LA_1LE0RB_1LF1LE_1LC0LD: rename A→E, B→F, C→C, D→A, E→B, F→D and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state D, in a mirror
  • 1RB0RE_1RC0RC_1LD---_0LB1LE_1RF0LD_1RA1RF: rename A→F, B→A, C→B, D→C, E→D, F→E; it is this table started in state B
  • 1RB0RB_1LC---_0LA1LD_1RE0LC_1RF1RE_1RA0RD: rename A→E, B→F, C→A, D→B, E→C, F→D; it is this table started in state C
  • 1RB0LF_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_1RE0RE_1LF---_0LD1LA: rename A→B, B→C, C→D, D→E, E→F, F→A; it is this table started in state F

summary: The head sweeps the whole left part of the tape; the tape is a list of blocks of 1s separated by single 0s whose lengths look geometrically distributed, and the leftmost block grows by 4 per sweep until it is broken up. Observed only; open.
